problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the annual budget across 13 infrastructure projects to maximize the total expected community benefit.  
The profile of each project is as follows:  
* Project A: expected benefit is 0.092, disruption index is 0.237, allocation bounds [0.020, 0.542]  
* Project B: expected benefit is 0.138, disruption index is 0.158, allocation bounds [0.002, 0.303]  
* Project C: expected benefit is 0.072, disruption index is 0.213, allocation bounds [0.070, 0.405]  
* Project D: expected benefit is 0.193, disruption index is 0.188, allocation bounds [0.092, 0.604]  
* Project E: expected benefit is 0.030, disruption index is 0.205, allocation bounds [0.055, 0.635]  
* Project F: expected benefit is 0.159, disruption index is 0.114, allocation bounds [0.073, 0.602]  
* Project G: expected benefit is 0.052, disruption index is 0.200, allocation bounds [0.056, 0.504]  
* Project H: expected benefit is 0.109, disruption index is 0.293, allocation bounds [0.058, 0.370]  
* Project I: expected benefit is 0.022, disruption index is 0.035, allocation bounds [0.035, 0.608]  
* Project J: expected benefit is 0.173, disruption index is 0.090, allocation bounds [0.082, 0.455]  
* Project K: expected benefit is 0.188, disruption index is 0.126, allocation bounds [0.023, 0.623]  
* Project L: expected benefit is 0.113, disruption index is 0.204, allocation bounds [0.096, 0.776]  
* Project M: expected benefit is 0.055, disruption index is 0.128, allocation bounds [0.045, 0.450]  

Each project must receive a fraction of the total budget within its specified bounds, and the sum of all budget fractions must equal one.  
To ensure rapid implementation, the group of quick-start projects Q = {D, F, K, L} must together receive at least 0.365 of the total budget.  
Additionally, the overall disruption index of the portfolio must not exceed 0.215, and the total expected community benefit must be at least 0.079.  
Find the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total expected benefit while satisfying all constraints.
